newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK 1996 gold imports drop to 208 tonnes from 259T.
newsitem.headline: HK 1996 gold imports drop to 208 tonnes from 259T.

text.p: Hong Kong imports of gold in unwrought, semi-manufactured or powder form and of gold coins fell to 208.18 tonnes in 1996 from about 259 tonnes in 1995, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department figures showed.
Excluding coins, imports of gold, unwrought or in semi-manufactured or powder form, fell to 207.56 tonnes, down from 258.97 tonnes in 1995.
Imports totalled 217.53 tonnes of gold and re-exports, 9.98 tonnes.
South Korea supplied about half of Hong Kong's gold imports in 1996, followed by Britain and South Africa which supplied 15 percent and 12 percent respectively.
About 35.7 percent of Hong Kong's re-exports in 1996 went to South Korea, 23 percent to Taiwan and 16.7 percent to China.
This compares with about 20 percent to South Korea, 20 percent to Taiwan, 14.8 percent to Malaysia and 14 percent to China in 1995.
In 1996, Hong Kong imported 2.13 tonnes of gold coins. Re-exports totalled 1.49 tonnes leaving a balance of 0.63 tonnes compared with 0.04 tonnes in 1995.
Canada was the largest supplier of gold coins in 1995, accounting for 36 percent, followed by China, which supplied 20 percent and the United States with 13 percent.
Switzerland and Germany were the leading buyers of coins from Hong Kong.
China supplied 32 percent of gold coins in 1996, followed by Australia and Canada, which supplied 31 percent and 27 percent.
